events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, Is Executed
events.description: After nearly 19 years of imprisonment in England, Mary, Queen of Scots, was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle in Northamptonshire. Her cousin Elizabeth I had signed the death warrant only reluctantly, after Mary was linked to plots against the English crown.
events.significance: The execution ended a long rivalry between two queens. It also cleared the way for the Stuart line to inherit the English throne through Mary's son, James VI and I.

events.title: Royal Charter Founds the College of William & Mary
events.description: King William III and Queen Mary II issued the royal charter establishing the College of William & Mary in colonial Virginia.
events.significance: It became the second-oldest institution of higher education in the American colonies. It went on to educate several of the nation's founding leaders.

events.title: Jules Verne Is Born
events.description: Jules Verne was born in the busy port city of Nantes, France. As a boy he sailed on the Loire River and dreamed of the sea. Those dreams later shaped his adventure novels.
events.significance: Verne helped found modern science fiction with works such as Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas and Around the World in Eighty Days. He remains one of the most widely translated authors in the world.

events.title: Japan Opens the Russo-Japanese War at Port Arthur
events.description: Japan declared war on Russia and launched a surprise torpedo attack on the Russian fleet at Port Arthur. The declaration did not reach Saint Petersburg until the next day.
events.significance: The attack began a conflict that ended in a Japanese victory. It marked the arrival of Japan as a major world military power and shook confidence in the Russian Empire.
